Project_Description: Three-tool image indexing/grouping/viewing suite: Cli_Image_Scanner (metadata+phash+exif indexer), CLI_Image_Grouper (dup/group builder), group_viewer (Flask group browser).

Initial build. Session mgmt (New/List/Sel/Del), Drive-Scan/Dir-Scan mode lock, Start-Scan/Stop-Scan with 10-image batch commit and resume-by-skip, MFDB image index (27 fields incl. 4-way phash + sha256 + exif), Field Map Cache used exclusively (no positional Values[] access). Core library family (full, incl. transitive deps discovered at runtime: bejson_errors, bejson_path_guard) copied into lib/Core/. Assumptions stated in file header and delivery message pending user confirmation.
Delivery 2/3: CLI_Image_Grouper.py

Added grouper tool. Phase 1 sha256 dedup pass into new GroupIndex entity (is_duplicate flag, no group_id yet), Phase 2 resumable phash Hamming clustering (threshold 10/64 bits) that promotes each 2+-member cluster into its own dedicated per-group MFDB entity inside sessions/<id>/groups/, folding in exact-hash duplicates of any clustered member. View-Group copies members to a temp image_holder/; Del-Group removes the group entity and reverts member rows to ungrouped. Verified end-to-end: exact-copy + 90-degree-rotated near-dup correctly clustered together, unrelated image stayed ungrouped.
Delivery 3/3: group_viewer.py

Added Flask review UI (BECSS-styled: header-command + sidebar-action-grid + footer-links + feed-gallery/data-table components). Implements the full common-sense dedup workflow confirmed with the user: soft-delete-only trash (sessions/<id>/trash/ + trash_log, permanent removal only via explicit Empty Trash), server-side staged-action review queue (trash/move/copy queue then Commit/Discard, nothing executes on a single click), groups list sorted by reclaimable-space descending with resolved/unresolved tracking, exact-sha256-duplicate tile collapsing (+N identical copies badge) vs full lightbox compare for phash near-dups, one-click Keep-Highest-Res/Newest/Oldest/Largest-File auto-keep strategies that stage (not commit) trash for the rest, select-all/invert/clear on the grid, per-image remove-from-group and per-group ungroup-all false-positive escapes, mobile long-press + desktop right-click context menu, and a built-in file browser for move/copy destinations. Move actions propagate the new file_path to both the group entity and the original ImageRecord index so neither goes stale; copy actions leave the index untouched. Verified end-to-end via Flask test client: exact-dup collapse (2->1 tile +badge), auto-keep staging + commit + trash-log + Empty-Trash permanent removal, group auto-dissolve below 2 members (both on commit and on remove_member), move with dual-index path propagation, file browser directory listing, and graceful handling of an unknown/empty session. Fresh libraries_104.zip upload diffed byte-identical against the Core lib already in lib/Core - no update needed.

Delivery 7: Audit remediation - Critical + High severity

User supplied a third-party 26-item audit report; verified every claim against actual source before acting (per standing practice), rather than trusting it - 25/26 confirmed real, L1 ('committed counter only increments for copy') confirmed FALSE by reading the code and by an earlier empirical test in this same session (trash-only commit already correctly returned committed=2). Fixed, in priority order per user's explicit 'critical and high first': S1 (path traversal on /api/browse) + S2 (arbitrary file disclosure via /image,/thumb) + S5 (unvalidated move/copy destinations) - added session-aware path containment (path_is_allowed()/session_allowed_roots(), config key viewer_allowed_roots, additive to the shared config so Cli_Image_Scanner.py's own ensure_config() is untouched) enforced on /api/browse, /image, /thumb, /api/stage (reject at stage time), and /api/stage/commit (re-validated at commit time, defense in depth). S3 (unauthenticated, 0.0.0.0-bound Flask app) - added a shared-secret token (config key viewer_api_token, auto-generated) required via X-API-Token header or ?token= on every route via before_request (the page shell itself is gated too, since it embeds the token - otherwise anyone could load / and read the token straight out of the HTML). Default bind changed to 127.0.0.1; --lan flag opts into 0.0.0.0 with an explicit printed warning. Menu_Image_Suite.py's direct app.run() call updated to match, plus the token URL is now printed on launch either way. S4 (stored XSS via innerHTML) - rewrote the lightbox (file_path, EXIF camera_model) and file-browser directory listing (entry.name) to use textContent/DOM text nodes instead of innerHTML string interpolation for every untrusted value. L2 (config batch_write_size never read) - cmd_start_scan now actually reads it, with a validated fallback to the module default. L3 (greedy phash clustering only compared candidates to the seed, order-dependent) - changed to a proper single-linkage fixpoint (a candidate joins if within threshold of ANY current cluster member, re-scanned until nothing new joins). L4 (temp file leak in build_image_record on exception) - wrapped in try/finally so the working copy is always unlinked regardless of what fails. L5 (right-click move/copy silently clobbered the grid's multi-selection) - introduced a separate pendingMoveCopyUuids snapshot so the context menu's single-image action no longer touches selectedRecordUuids. L6 (both CLI_Image_Grouper.py and group_viewer.py imported underscore-prefixed private mfdb_core internals, bypassing the library's own ResilientPIDLock) - replaced every call site with the public, lock-protected mfdb_core_update_entity_record/mfdb_core_remove_entity_record API; this was a bigger finding than 'fragile to refactor' as originally flagged, since the private-function path also skipped locking entirely. R4 (missing-Flask crash in the menu's Launch Viewer action) fixed alongside S3 as part of the same code path. Also opportunistically fixed while touching app.js for S4/B5: B5 (no fetch error handling - added try/catch + a toast notification on failure) and B6 (no debounce on the group filter input - added 250ms debounce), since both were trivial and in the same file. Medium/Low items not covered in this pass (B1-B3, B7-B9, R1-R3, R6) are queued for the follow-up pass the user indicated they still want. Verified via Flask test client: no-token/wrong-token 403 on both API routes and the page shell, correct-token 200, path traversal to /etc blocked with correct-token, legit session-scoped path (session's own Dir-Scan target, not just the global drive_scan_root) allowed, image/thumb serving gated, stage-time destination containment rejecting /etc and accepting a subdir of the session's own scan target, full commit executing and moving the file correctly through the new validated path. Full four-tool regression re-run through Menu_Image_Suite.py end-to-end with no tracebacks.
Delivery 8: Playwright in-depth audit + 'page fails to load' fix

User reported the viewer page failing to load. Ran a real Playwright audit against the live server (chromium, 15 checks covering: token gate, groups list, group detail, thumbnail actual pixel load via naturalWidth, lightbox, right-click context menu, all 14 toolbar buttons present, Select All, and the file-browser modal) rather than guessing at the cause. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: hitting the bare / URL (no ?token=) returned Flask's raw 403 page, which the S3 fix from the previous delivery introduced - a bookmarked URL, a dropped query string, or just visiting / directly looked exactly like a broken page. Fixed by splitting '/' out of the blanket before_request gate and having index() itself decide: valid token -> the real app (unchanged, still embeds the real token so it must still be checked); missing/invalid token -> a new minimal login.html template that leaks no session/group data, just a token-entry form. Client-side JS on both pages persists the token to localStorage on success and auto-redirects through it on repeat visits, so this only prompts once per browser. SECOND BUG FOUND VIA THE AUDIT (not reported by the user): at a real mobile viewport (390x844, matching the stated Android target), the entire BECSS sidebar - holding Refresh, Empty Trash, and critically Back-to-Groups - is display:none, and the hamburger menu's mobile-sidebar drawer was being built completely empty. Net effect: on an actual phone, once a group is opened there was no way back to the group list without reloading the page. Fixed by moving Back-to-Groups into the always-visible header (core navigation, not a secondary action) and populating the mobile drawer with working Refresh/Empty Trash duplicates wired to the same handlers as the desktop sidebar buttons. Verified via Playwright at 390px: Back button visible and functional, hamburger drawer opens with working buttons. THIRD BUG FOUND VIA THE AUDIT: /api/browse had no fallback when the configured drive_scan_root doesn't exist/isn't reachable (surfaced in the dev sandbox as /storage/emulated/0 not existing, but the same failure mode hits real Android before termux-setup-storage has been run) - it just 400'd with a bare technical message. Fixed to fall back to the current session's own known-good Dir-Scan target when the configured root is unreachable, and to return an actionable error message (mentions termux-setup-storage) instead of a bare 'not a directory'. Final re-run: all 15 Playwright checks pass, zero console errors, zero console warnings, zero uncaught JS exceptions, zero failed/non-2xx network requests.
Delivery 9: 'API error' on delete/move fixed (root cause confirmed by live reproduction, not guessed)

User reported delete/move 'API errors' with no other detail and no time for speculative fixes, so reproduced the real pipeline end-to-end (fresh scan session, real exact-dup group, real Flask server, real HTTP calls against /api/stage and /api/stage/commit) instead of guessing. Ruled out two plausible-looking theories by testing them directly: batched multi-item trash commits (3 staged removals in one group, one commit call) succeeded cleanly with no error, and move-destination containment (path_is_allowed on dest_dir) is unreachable via the actual file-browser picker since /api/browse already enforces the same containment on every navigation step, so a real user can never select a blocked destination. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED BY REPRODUCTION: the single most common workflow - a 2-member exact-duplicate group, trash the dup, keep 1 - causes the group to auto-dissolve server-side (_dissolve_if_undersized, by design, working correctly). But app.js's commit handler unconditionally called openGroup(currentGroupId) afterward to refresh the view; against a just-dissolved group that 404s, and openGroup's `if (!data) return;` swallows it after getJSON already threw a 'Request failed (404)' toast - so the trash/move genuinely succeeds server-side but the user sees a scary error and a stale, unrefreshed tile grid. Fixed by having _dissolve_if_undersized (group_viewer.py) return whether it actually dissolved the group, api_stage_commit collecting those into a new dissolved_groups field in its response, and app.js's commit handler checking currentGroupId against that list before deciding to reopen the group vs. fall back to the group list. Verified by re-running the exact failing scenario against the patched server: commit response now correctly reports dissolved_groups:[<the group's id>] instead of the client blindly 404ing on the next fetch.

Delivery 11: Token-entry keyboard flicker loop fixed (root cause confirmed by code + live server test)

User reported (garbled/dictated report): entering the access token on the login page made the Android keyboard 'open and close over and over' so they couldn't type it, and once they got in 'one time' thumbnails were broken. ROOT CAUSE (login.html): the page unconditionally redirected to /?token=<localStorage value> on every load with zero validation that the saved token was ever correct - the token regenerates every group_viewer.py launch, so any stale/mistyped saved token creates an infinite loop: reload -> autofocus opens the keyboard -> the script immediately fires window.location.replace() with the same bad token -> page navigates away -> keyboard closes -> server rejects the bad token and re-serves login.html -> reload -> repeat forever, with no stable window to type a correction. This also plausibly explains the broken thumbnails as a downstream symptom (images mid-fetch getting killed by the next reload), not a separate bug - left alone since /thumb and /image already correctly source their URLs from the server-embedded, verified-correct token (window.GV_API_TOKEN), not from localStorage, so they can only 403/break while the surrounding page itself is unstable. FIX: login.html now checks whether a token param is already present in the current URL before redirecting - if so, the server just rejected that exact token (a valid one would have rendered the app page instead), so the script clears the stale localStorage entry and lets the form render normally instead of redirecting again. Verified against the real running server: a bad token in the URL now serves login.html with the tokenForm intact (loop broken, confirmed via grep for the new localStorage.removeItem call in the response), a good token still serves the real app page (GV_API_TOKEN embedded, no login form) - existing correct-token flow is untouched.
